adoption_var_note: g_true (calendar year, same units as year; NA = never-adopting state) in sample_nov2_adoption.rds: UTSA adoption year of the firm's HQ state, so firms in 1980-1998 adopter states are pre-sample adopters with true event time (rel up to 29) and firms in 2012/2013/2018 adopter states have leads, as in the authors' eventdd timevar. treat_var utsa_dummy is kept so run_spec drops the 105 switch-off rows. Run_spec semantics (code-agent, Nov 2): adoption_var only moves the date of units that treat_var treats; firms in states adopting after 2009 (2012/2013/2018) and 24 other firms whose date falls after their last row stay never-treated (the authors give the post-2009 adopters lead dummies). Checked with the data-preparation block of the current run_spec.R (no stop; 1,474 units dated earlier, 1,462 pre-sample).

event_structure.source: ABH_main_tests.do line 195: eventdd gwavg_erp_d_adopted, timevar(time_relative_to_utsa) method(hdfe, absorb(gvkey sic2#year) cluster(group_state_id)) lags(4) leads(4) accum baseline(-1). time_relative_to_utsa = year - utsa_year of the firm's CURRENT HQ state (checked on every row); with g = the firm's first UTSA year, rel = t - g = time_relative_to_utsa (years 1999-2009 consecutive). accum: relative times <= -4 and >= 4 are accumulated into the end bins, so bins = (<= -4), -3, -2, 0, 1, 2, 3, (>= 4), reference -1; firms in never-adopting states (missing timevar) have all indicators zero. Every relative time is in a bin or the reference (nothing uncovered). True relative time: firms in states that adopted 1980-1998 enter at rel 1..29 (mostly the >= 4 bin; 1995-1998 adopters at +1..+3 in 1999-2002) and firms in states adopting 2012/2013/2018 at leads -3..-19 -> adoption_var. Summaries: post rel 0..3, pre rel -3..-2 (the accumulated end bins, drawn in a different colour in Figure 2, are not averaged).

replication_status: exact (package reconstructed: the eventdd-equivalent reghdfe regression is reproduced identically in Stata MP 16.1 and fixest; Figure 2 matched visually against the article; figure-only, no printed value; verified Nov 4 2026)
notes: Same sample, FE and clustering as Table 2 column 1. Authors' relative time = year - utsa_year of the firm's current HQ state: never-adopting states (1,211 rows) are the reference group; always-treated states (adopted 1980-1998) enter at their true relative time (1995-1998 adopters appear in bins +1 to +3 in 1999-2002, all others in the +4 bin); states adopting in 2012-2018 appear in the lead bins. run_spec.R instead derives relative time from the firm-level first year with utsa_dummy = 1, so the 1,478 always-treated firms sit at relative time 0..4 in 1999-2003 and drop into the +5 bin afterwards, and post-2009 adopters are never-treated controls. Endpoint bins in the runner are -5 and +5 (outside the averaging window), versus the authors' accumulated -4 and +4. The 105 switch-off rows are dropped by the runner. These differences are recorded as deviations; the runner's post/pre averages are therefore not expected to equal the equal-weight averages of the authors' bins (post 0.0469, pre -0.0076 in raw units; 0.1213 and -0.0196 in SD units with SD 0.38676). NOV 2 AUDIT (supersedes the timing deviation above): event_structure keeps eventdd's bins (<= -4, -3, -2, 0..3, >= 4; ref -1) and adoption_var = g_true gives every firm its true first UTSA year, so firms in states that adopted 1980-1998 enter at their true relative time (pre-sample adopters: 1,462 firms; always-treated for DiD-averaging and imputation) and firms in states adopting 2012/2013/2018 get lead indicators (379 firms; untreated within the sample). data_path = sample_nov2_adoption.rds (package dta columns needed by this spec plus g_true, mover, switch_off; built by ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2021.03484/nov2_build_verify.R). Rule for g_true: firms in one HQ state (2,057) get their state's utsa_year; for the 107 HQ movers, treated at entry -> the entry state's utsa_year, observed untreated first -> the later of the state's year and the year after the last untreated row (= move year for the 24 firms moving into an already-treated state), never treated -> utsa_year of the last observed state. treat_var utsa_dummy is kept so run_spec drops the 105 switch-off rows (20 firms). Residual differences from the authors' Figure 2 regression: the switch-off rows and movers' single date (authors: current state's date each year). Pipeline-rule TWFE (raw): post_summary 0.0515170 (0.0224521), pre_summary 0.0051360 (0.0196656); treating the post-sample adopters as never-treated instead changes the post average to 0.0515327.
